title: Banking in Spain: choose the account you actually need
status: Bank requirements vary; EU payment rights still apply
intro: Start with the use case, then choose an account and prepare the bank's identity and source-of-funds checks. A Spanish IBAN can be convenient, but an EU account cannot be rejected for a SEPA payment merely because it is from another EU country.

items.label: 1. Decide if you need a Spanish account
items.text: For salary, rent and direct debits, first check whether your existing SEPA account already works. A local account may still be convenient for branch service, cash and Spanish banking products.

items.label: 2. Choose a regulated provider
items.text: Compare Spanish banks and authorised payment providers. Ordinary banks generally decide whether to open a standard account, while eligible customers have separate rights to request a basic payment account.

items.label: 3. Choose the right account status
items.text: Ask whether the bank is opening a resident, non-resident, ordinary current or basic payment account. Do not claim resident status you cannot document; product names and requirements differ by bank.

items.label: 4. Complete the bank's KYC onboarding
items.text: There is no single government form for a normal bank account. Complete the bank's application, tax-residence declarations and anti-money-laundering questions accurately.

items.label: 5. Prepare identity and financial evidence
bullets: EU citizen: passport or national ID plus NIE may be requested
Non-EU citizen: TIE is commonly used for identification
Non-residents may be asked to prove non-resident status
Proof of address, income/employment and source of funds may be requested

items.label: 6. Check the account before using it
bullets: Read fees, card and transfer conditions before signing
Confirm the IBAN and direct-debit setup you will use
Keep evidence of source of funds available
If an EU IBAN is rejected only because of its country code, check the EU IBAN-discrimination rules
